title: Policy evaluation (the prediction problem)
summary: Computing v_π for a given policy π. With known dynamics, the Bellman equation is a system of |S| linear equations in |S| unknowns; v_π exists and is unique if γ < 1 or every state eventually terminates under π.

title: Iterative policy evaluation
summary: Start from an arbitrary v_0 (terminal value 0) and repeatedly apply the Bellman equation as an update to every state (a full backup) until the largest change in a sweep falls below a small threshold θ. The in-place version overwrites values as it goes and usually converges faster.

title: 4×4 gridworld under the equiprobable random policy
summary: Fourteen nonterminal states, one terminal state drawn in two corners, deterministic moves that stay put at the edge, reward −1 per step, undiscounted. Iterative policy evaluation converges to v_π, the negated expected number of steps to termination.

title: Policy improvement
summary: Acting greedily with respect to $v_\pi$, choosing $\operatorname{argmax}_a q_\pi(s, a)$ in every state (4.9), gives a policy at least as good as $\pi$ everywhere. That is the policy improvement theorem (4.7)–(4.8). If the greedy policy is no better, $\pi$ was already optimal.

title: Policy iteration
summary: Alternate full policy evaluation and greedy improvement, $\pi_0 \to v_{\pi_0} \to \pi_1 \to v_{\pi_1} \to \cdots$, until the policy stops changing. A finite MDP has finitely many policies, so this ends at an optimal policy, often after very few iterations.

title: Value iteration
summary: Policy iteration with evaluation cut to a single sweep: back up each state with the maximum over actions (4.10). This turns the Bellman optimality equation into an update rule, and $v_k$ converges to $v_*$. A greedy policy is read off at the end.
